facts.text: LIBERO is designed for studying knowledge transfer in multitask and lifelong robot learning
LIBERO provides 130 tasks grouped into four task suites: LIBERO-Spatial, LIBERO-Object, LIBERO-Goal and LIBERO-100
The README creates OffScreenRenderEnv with a 128x128 camera, calls env.seed(0) and then env.reset()
The README steps the environment with a seven-element zero action and unpacks obs, reward, done, info
The README says only a sparse reward is supported: +1 when the task is finished
The package is published as libero and requires Python >=3.8
The runtime pins robosuite==1.4.0 and bddl==1.0.1
The entry class is registered with @register_problem and subclasses BDDLBaseDomain
The constructor requires bddl_file_name and robots and parses the BDDL problem from that file
The constructor parses the BDDL problem file into parsed_problem
reward is 0.0, or 1.0 when _check_success returns true
step calls the robosuite step and then replaces done with _check_success
The coffee-table success check ANDs every predicate of the parsed goal_state
The base constructor defaults to camera observations (use_camera_obs=True)
The default camera is agentview at 256x256 pixels
get_robot_state_vector concatenates robot0_gripper_qpos, robot0_eef_pos and robot0_eef_quat
language_instruction returns the parsed problem's language string

determinism.notes: the upstream seed calls np.random.seed(seed) (bddl_base_domain.py:162-163) and the placement samplers draw from numpy's generator; the fake reseeds Python's random.Random, so a seed repeats the fake's state hashes but the fake and upstream do not share a random stream or a physics model

gaps: the fake backend is a physics-free stand-in: it keeps three end-effector coordinates and a tick count, moves them by a placeholder gain, and integrates no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, actuators, sensors, cameras or noise; the upstream environment builds a robosuite/MuJoCo world

the observation is a placeholder dictionary with the three robot keys the clone's get_robot_state_vector names (bddl_base_domain.py:826-829); the real observation also carries object observations and the agentview/robot0_eye_in_hand camera images that the constructor enables by default (bddl_base_domain.py:51 and :67-69), and its array lengths depend on the BDDL task and the camera configuration

there is no fixed timestep in the clone: control_freq is a constructor option with default 20 (bddl_base_domain.py:63) and the physics step comes from the robosuite model, so timestep_ms is 0 and ticks count control steps, not physics steps

the action vector's shape is a constructor option (the wrapper's default controller is OSC_POSE, env_wrapper.py:17); the fake accepts any non-empty numeric vector and the README example uses seven zeros (README.md:131)
the BDDL file selects the objects, placements and goal predicates; the fake parses no BDDL file and never reports success (done is always false and reward is always 0.0)
snapshot and restore are not offered by this package
MuJoCo, robosuite and bddl were not installed and the upstream environment was never run, so no trajectory or observation of this package was compared with it
no physical device is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware
